sentences.text: Ferenceratops is diagnosed by a unique combination of anatomical characters that set it apart from other taxa.
It possesses a narrow scapula with a strap-like blade and a prominent, upwardly concave acromial process.
The ischium, a bone of the pelvis, is gently curved and lacks an obturator process.
No ornithopod synapomorphies—shared derived traits of that group—were identified in the holotype, while several features align with ceratopsians.
The genus Ferenceratops was erected by Maidment and colleagues in 2026.
Its name derives from the birth name of Baron Franz Nopcsa, who first described the material in 1928.
The holotype, originally described as Zalmoxes shqiperorum, is a partial skeleton now housed at the Natural History Museum in London.
The specific epithet shqiperorum honors the people of Shqiperia, the Albanian name for their nation.
Fossils once assigned to the ornithopod Zalmoxes were reinterpreted as belonging to Ferenceratops after phylogenetic work showed the placement of Z. robustus to be unstable.
A new partial skull referable to Ajkaceratops, described in 2026, helped clarify Ferenceratops’s identity.
Maidment et al. recognized only a single referred specimen—a pelvis (UBB SPZ-2)—as assignable to Ferenceratops, while most other material lacked overlap with the holotype.
The fossils come from the Sânpetru and Densuș-Ciula formations in Romania.
Ferenceratops shared its habitat with titanosaurian sauropods and feathered theropods such as Balaur and Elopteryx.
The same formation also yielded the ankylosaur Struthiosaurus and the hadrosauromorph Telmatosaurus.
Other members of the ecosystem included the giant pterosaur Hatzegopteryx, various crocodilians, snakes, lizards, turtles, birds, mammals, amphibians, and fish.
Ferenceratops is placed within Ceratopsia, the horned-dinosaur clade, based on phylogenetic analysis by Maidment et al. in 2026.
Ceratopsia belongs to the larger ornithischian group Ornithischia, the ‘bird-hipped’ dinosaurs.
Phylogenetic studies suggest it is a close relative of Ajkaceratops and part of a distinct European ceratopsian lineage.
Ferenceratops lived during the Late Cretaceous Maastrichtian stage, between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
The environment was subtropical with alternating rainy and dry seasons, and isotope evidence points to a dry woodland setting with mean annual temperatures of 20 to 25 °C.
Some researchers argue that material previously assigned to rhabdodontids like Zalmoxes may actually represent multiple distinct taxa, encompassing both iguanodonts and ceratopsians.
There is also ongoing discussion about whether Ferenceratops should be placed within Rhabdodontidae or Ceratopsia, given its historical classification as an ornithopod.
